speaker: Swami Sivananda
title: Humility in overcoming lower nature
text: If you want to drink water at the tap, you will have to bend yourself. Even so, if you want to drink the spiritual nectar of immortality which flows from the holy lips of the Guru, you will have to be an embodiment of humility and meekness. One's individual ego, preconceived notions, pet ideas and prejudices, and selfish interests should be given up. All these stand in the way of carrying out instructions.
modern_interpretation: To truly absorb profound wisdom and grow, you must adopt a stance of genuine openness and humility, much like bending to drink from a tap. This means consciously setting aside your personal biases, cherished opinions, defensiveness, and self-serving motives. These mental barriers prevent you from fully internalizing and acting upon valuable guidance.
summary: To receive profound spiritual wisdom, one must cultivate deep humility and meekness, letting go of individual ego, preconceived notions, prejudices, and selfish interests, as these obstruct the absorption and application of divine instructions.
actionable_advice: The next time you encounter a new teaching or perspective, consciously pause and identify any immediate resistance, pet ideas, or preconceived notions you hold, and then attempt to set them aside to truly listen.
embedding_ready_text: Swami Sivananda teaches that just as one must bend to drink water, profound spiritual wisdom requires deep humility and meekness. This means actively surrendering the individual ego, preconceived notions, pet ideas, prejudices, and selfish interests that otherwise block the absorption of divine instructions. This wisdom addresses pride, ego-resistance, and closed-mindedness, guiding towards receptivity and openness. It is transformative advice for self-growth and spiritual development, urging us to consciously set aside our biases to truly learn and evolve.
